newsitem.title: ROMANIA: FRANCE, ITALY, SPAIN BACK ROMANIA NATO BID - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: FRANCE, ITALY, SPAIN BACK ROMANIA NATO BID - MINISTER.

text.p: France, Italy and Spain will support Romania's bid to achieve fast admission into NATO, Defence Minister Victor Babiuc said on Wednesday.
"Italy and France reiterated their support for our access in a first wave of NATO's expansion. Spain expressed the same position," Babiuc told a news conference.
Babiuc made the remarks after a visit last week to Paris Rome and Madrid. He also met NATO Secretary General Javier Solana in Brussels.

His tour was part of diplomatic efforts by Bucharest over the past months to persuade the Western alliance to accept Romania in the first wave of a planned enlargement, expected to be announced at a NATO summit in Madrid this summer.
"The tour was useful as we got the three countries' open and clear support," he said. "I hope this achievement will play an important role at the Madrid summit".

Babiuc said a recent poll showed 95 percent of the army officers favoured Romania's integration into NATO. It also showed some 60 percent of the military agreed with the establishement of NATO bases in the country, he said.

President Emil Constantinescu, during a visit to the Czech Republic earlier this week, said Romania met all NATO membership criteria related to democracy and human rights. He said he saw no obstacles to full membership other than the costs for the upgrading of the country's military equipment.
Romania was the first East Europen country to sign for NATO's Partnership for Peace programme.
